result.caveats: All 12 panels are confirmed exposed fastener (screw-down) profiles per McElroy's own product pages under mcelroymetal.com/exposed-fastener-panels (hub page verified 2026-08-19). McElroy's concealed-fastener lines (Medallion-Lok, Maxima, Meridian, Matrix, Marquee/flush wall, Mirage, etc.) were excluded per instructions. Notes: (1) Multi-Rib rib height is 1-3/16 in. per its spec page even though marketing copy elsewhere says 1-1/4 in.; both Multi-Rib and R-Panel offer purlin-bearing (PBR) leg versions. (2) U-Panel rib height is listed as 47/64 in. (~0.73 in.). (3) Mega-Rib coverage is 28.8 in. standard; a 36 in. version is produced only at the Adelanto, CA facility in 26 GA. (4) The category hub page advertises gauges 29-24 GA across the line with Kynar 500 PVDF or SMP finishes; individual product pages list narrower standard gauge offerings, which are what is recorded per panel. (5) Multi-V places fasteners in the valleys to minimize their appearance but is still an exposed fastener panel. (6) Mesa is a patent-protected geometry; the generic classification 'low-profile trapezoidal rib / ag-panel class' is an approximation since no exact industry-generic equivalent exists. (7) Modern-Rib mimics standing seam aesthetics but attaches through the flat with exposed screws; no exact single generic term exists for this class.

result.caveats: Company identification: settled on the TEXAS company, Quality Metals at saqualitymetals.com — a panel/coil manufacturer-supplier headquartered in San Antonio with locations in Dallas (11569 Goodnight Ln, Dallas, TX 75229, (972) 331-6800), Houston, and McAllen, selling painted steel panels, coil, and flats to contractors across Texas; this is the plausible DFW-area shop supplier. Ruled out: qualitymetalsinc.com (Quality Metals Inc., St. Paul, MN) is a flat-rolled sheet/coil distributor with NO roll-formed panel products; also ruled out Quality Metals Inc. of Florida (an installer/fabricator) and Quality Metal Roofing (qualitymetal.us, KY/WV). Panel notes: (1) The site's metal-panels index listed HP-Panel (/qm-hp/) and H1-Panel (/qm-h1/) alongside exposed-fastener products, but their product pages describe them as CONCEALED-fastener "Precision Series" wall/roof systems (hidden fasteners, no visible screws), so they were excluded; verify before adding. (2) Quality Metals' AG-Panel page states 12 in. o.c. rib spacing, wider than the typical 9 in. o.c. ag/tuff-rib profile — spec kept as published. (3) The site also offers standing seam/concealed systems (SL-150, SLZ-150, NS-100/NS-150 nail strip, ML-100/150/200/300, Flush Panel) and Wakefield Bridge steel shingles, all excluded per scope. (4) Detailed spec-sheet PDFs were not fetched; dimensions come from the product pages' stated specs.

result.caveats: All dimensions verified from Petersen's own PAC-CLAD spec sheets (rev 7/26) downloaded from pac-clad.com product pages. This is PAC-CLAD's complete current exposed fastener lineup; everything else they make (Snap-Clad, Tite-Loc/Tite-Loc Plus, PAC-150, T-250, Precision Series Box Rib/Highline/HWP, flush/reveal, board & batten, composite ACM, insulated metal panels) is concealed fastener and excluded. Notes: (1) Corrugated coverage is lap-dependent — 7/8" Corrugated covers 37.33" as siding (1 lapped rib) and 34.67" as roofing (2 lapped ribs); 1/2" Corrugated covers 42.67" as siding and 40" with a 2-rib roofing lap; I listed 34.67" (roof) for the 7/8" and 42.67" (wall) for the 1/2" since Petersen groups the 1/2" with wall/equipment-screen panels. (2) Petersen explicitly states M-36, M-42, and 1/2" Corrugated are for wall/equipment-screen use and that M-panels are "not intended for... structural roof applications"; M-42 is made only in the Tyler, TX plant. (3) On the M-panel spec sheet the 1" (M-42) and 1-1/32" (M-36) figures are rib-top widths, not heights — rib height is 3/4" per the SPECS block. (4) Panel lengths: up to 30' steel, 22' aluminum; precut shorts 5'-0" min (3'-0" on M-42); most profiles can be perforated. (5) Min slope figures (7.2 panel ~2:12; 7/8" corrugated ~2.5:12) come from secondary PAC literature summaries, not the spec sheets — confirm with Petersen. (6) A former R-41 panel URL now redirects to R-36; R-41 appears discontinued and is omitted.

result.caveats: All 7 panels confirmed exposed fastener from Drexel's own data sheets: the DMC Wall Series sheets (DM-12585 R-Panel, DM-12586 M-Panel, DM-12588 7.2 Rib, DM-12591 Corrugated) each print an "EXPOSED FASTENER" family chart listing R-36, M-42, M-36, 7.2, 1/2" and 7/8" Corrugated; the 5V sheet (DM-16422) states "exposed fastener design." Details: (1) 5V rib height — the product page says 3/8" but the data-sheet drawing dimensions the crimp at 0.5"; 5V is also offered in a 20.5" nominal width besides 24". (2) Corrugated coverage listed is the siding coverage (1 lapped rib); roofing coverage with 2 lapped ribs is 34.67" for 7/8" (40" nominal sheet) and 40" for 1/2" (44.5" nominal sheet). (3) R-Panel coverage is 36" net / 41" overall including overlap; Drexel's old R-41 profile is marked DISCONTINUED on the family chart. (4) M-36/M-42 carry a note that they are "not intended for use in the construction of metal buildings or structural roof applications" — wall panels primarily; consult Drexel for roof use. (5) 7.2 Rib is sold under the Wall Series but the site lists walls/roofs applications (ICC-ES ESR-5838). Excluded as NOT exposed fastener: all DMC standing seam roof systems (100SS, 150SS/SL, 175S, 200S, 250T, 450, 450SL, 550S, Cap Seam), the NS nail-strip profiles (100NS, 150NS — fastener flange), FW1/FWQ100/FWQ150 flush panels, Board & Batten (fasteners concealed under batten, confirmed on product page), DMC 164 & 123 (clip or concealed fastener-flange, confirmed on data sheet DM-12578), Drexel Facade HL and Facade BR box-rib wall panels (clip or concealed fastener-flange, confirmed on data sheet DM-16222), and DMC 450 wall application.

result.caveats: All five panels are Berridge's official "Exposed Fastener Panel Systems" category (https://www.berridge.com/products/exposed-fastener-panel-systems/) — this is their complete exposed-fastener lineup; specs verified from Berridge's own data sheet PDFs. Notes: (1) S-Deck coverage is 32 in. OR 34-2/3 in. (two coverage options; only 32 in. fit the single numeric field); factory-curved S-Deck available (5 ft min radius). On roofs S-Deck installs vertical only. (2) Berridge calls their trapezoidal-rib panel simply "R" Panel (no purlin-bearing leg shown on the data sheet drawing, so "R-Panel" is more precise than "PBR"). (3) Double-Rib Panel is roof-only, vertical over solid sheathing; its geometry (1/2 in. V-type double ribs at 12 in. o.c., 24 in. coverage) is closest to the 5V-Crimp family but is not a true 5-crimp 5V — contractors would recognize it as a 5V-style/double-rib panel. (4) M-Panel rib spacing is a paired-rib module; the data sheet drawing dimensions (6 in. / 2-1/2 in. / 3-1/2 in., 1 in. rib tops) are reproduced as-is since a single o.c. number does not describe it. (5) Berridge's many wall/soffit/fascia panels (HR-16, HS-8, RS-series, FW-series, Vee-Panel, Board & Batten, BR-12, L-Panel, etc.) and all standing seam, batten, shingle, and tile systems are concealed-fastener and were excluded. Berridge does not list a U-Panel, ag/tuff-rib, 1/4 in. or 2-1/2 in. low-corrugated, or true 5V-Crimp product.
